turns.reply: The `@dataclass` decorator sets `__hash__` to `None` because it defines `__eq__`. I'll add an explicit `__hash__` to both classes. `Security.scopes` can be a list, so it gets converted to a tuple before hashing.

+++ b/fastapi/params.py
@@ -768,7 +768,14 @@
     use_cache: bool = True
     scope: Union[Literal["function", "request"], None] = None
 
+    def __hash__(self) -> int:
+        return hash((self.dependency, self.use_cache, self.scope))
+
 
 @dataclass
 class Security(Depends):
     scopes: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None
+
+    def __hash__(self) -> int:
+        scopes = tuple(self.scopes) if self.scopes is not None else None
+        return hash((self.dependency, self.use_cache, self.scope, scopes))

turns.reply:
I made `Depends()` and `Security()` hashable by adding explicit `__hash__` methods in `fastapi/params.py`, and submitted the patch.

The `@dataclass` decorator had set `__hash__` to `None` because the classes define `__eq__`. `Security` converts `scopes` to a tuple before hashing, since a list can't be hashed. A quick check confirmed both objects hash and `Depends(f) == Depends(f)` still holds, and `tests/test_dependency_cache.py` passes. I did not run a broader test suite.
